subject.title: fix(synology-chat): handle HEAD probe and return 200 on webhook ACK

question: Should Synology Chat webhook routes intentionally return unauthenticated 200 responses to HEAD liveness probes while keeping POST authentication and throttling unchanged?
rationale: The fix likely matches Synology delivery behavior, but the tokenless HEAD response exposes endpoint liveness and should be an explicit maintainer-owned boundary decision before landing.

options.title: Accept HEAD Liveness With Proof
options.body: Accept the tokenless HEAD 200 contract, require redacted Synology proof, and preserve current POST security guardrails during rebase or replacement.

options.title: Require Authenticated Probe Alternative
options.body: Keep the PR paused unless Synology can be configured to probe with credentials or another authenticated compatibility path is proven.

options.title: Replace The Branch
options.body: If the contributor cannot refresh and prove the branch, open a narrow maintainer replacement that credits this PR and keeps the canonical issue linked.

recommendation.title: Accept HEAD Liveness With Proof
recommendation.body: Accept the tokenless HEAD 200 contract, require redacted Synology proof, and preserve current POST security guardrails during rebase or replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows repeated maintenance of the Synology Chat webhook and gateway route surface.
